title: Reasoning in Two Dimensions: Quantifying Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness and Efficiency
abstract: arXiv:2611.27100v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning exposes intermediate steps, but a correct answer does not establish that an LLM relies on the dependence expressed by those steps or reasons efficiently. We operationalize CoT faithfulness and efficiency within a common framework. Specifically, we represent a CoT as a semantic reasoning graph and decompose the model's predictive dependence along two complementary axes: dependence explained by semantic support versus additional reasoning history, and dependence allocated to answer-reaching versus off-path reasoning. This decomposition yields global and step-level measures of unfaithfulness and inefficiency. Controlled interventions show that the proposed metrics respond to hidden dependence and induced off-path reasoning as intended. tldr: 该论文提出将思维链表示为语义推理图，并沿“语义支持对推理历史”与“通往答案对偏离路径”两个维度分解模型的预测依赖性，在同一框架下实现了对思维链非忠实性与低效性的全局及步骤级量化。
en_tdlr: This paper represents chain-of-thought as a semantic reasoning graph and decomposes the model's predictive dependence along two complementary axes—semantic support vs. reasoning history, and answer-reaching vs. off-path reasoning—yielding a unified framework to quantify CoT unfaithfulness and inefficiency at both global and step levels.
